justification: Changes the note shown under every council DCP rule whose words are not proven (about 3,000 rules); wrong, the note could cite a page that differs from the link beside it.

pre_impl.existing_data: regulatory_provisions quote_status, pdf_page, page_check, printed_page_label already served to every route that calls quoteNote
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: the page in the note must be the one printed beside the rule, so it reuses pageLabel() from lib/page-citation.ts rather than reading pdf_page
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: applies on read to every unproven council rule; nothing is written
pre_impl.external_source_error: no external source; a row with no located page gets the note without a page number
pre_impl.frontend_type: QuoteFields now extends PageFields (pdf_page, printed_page_label, page_check are optional fields already on the rows)
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: if the page label is missing the note still shows, without a page, so the rule is never presented as the council's words

functions.name: unprovenNote
functions.input: a served council rule row whose words are not proven, with its page fields
functions.output: Our reading — check the exact wording on <page label> of the council's plan, or the same without a page
functions.if_none: page not located or no page: the note without a page number

values.if_missing: the note without a page number

queries.purpose: none: the change is display text; listed because the report requires one entry
queries.where_clause: not applicable: no SQL is added or changed by this change
queries.if_zero: not applicable: no query is run here
queries.if_wrong: not applicable: no rows are read or written here

break_it.scenario: The note names PDF page 40 while the link beside the rule says page 12
break_it.what_happens: a reader would open the wrong page to check the council's exact wording
break_it.how: the note uses pageLabel(), the same function that prints the page beside the rule

break_it.scenario: A rule whose page was not located gets a page number in its note
break_it.what_happens: the note would point at a page that was never shown to hold the rule
break_it.how: PAGE_NOT_LOCATED and null labels give the note without a page

break_it.scenario: A proven rule shows the new unproven note
break_it.what_happens: the council's own words would be labelled as our reading and look unreliable
break_it.how: quoteNote returns QUOTE_NOTE_CONFIRMED first for every rule that shows the council's words

break_it.scenario: The old wording survives in one route that builds its own note
break_it.what_happens: pages of the site would disagree about what an unproven rule is called
break_it.how: every route calls quoteNote from lib/council-quote.ts; the old strings exist nowhere else

break_it.scenario: A statewide (LEP/SEPP) rule gets the council note
break_it.what_happens: a State rule would be called our reading of a council plan, which is wrong
break_it.how: quoteNote returns null when source_council is missing, unchanged by this change

break_it.scenario: none: the change is display text, yet a route's select list drops the page columns the note needs
break_it.what_happens: the note would lose its page number on that route while the link beside the rule still shows one
break_it.how: no query or select list is changed; the note reads only fields every route already sends

falsifiable_check.fails_when: the note keeps the old wording, cites a page other than pageLabel, or names a page that was not located
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Before this change the new tests fail: quoteNote returned 'Not yet checked against the council's PDF'.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: User decision 2026-10-13: wording option B, 'Our reading — check the exact wording on page 12 of the council's plan'.

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes: on the preview, open a property with an unproven council rule and read the note under it
